title: Take a terminal block from a person's hand, then snap it onto a loose DIN rail
instruction: Take the terminal block from the person's hand: grip it while they still hold it, so they can let go. Then press it straight down onto the DIN rail until it clicks, without knocking the rail out of place.
context: A person passing parts to a robot at a bench is routine in assembly cells; the robot has to receive them gently (no snatching, no pressing on the hand) before it can use them.
setup: On the table in front of the arms: a loose steel TS35 x 7.5 top-hat DIN rail, 240 mm long, 150 g, lying open side up and running left to right, its centre 0.30 m in front of the arm bases and 0.04 m right of their midline; fixed on it, a zinc end bracket near each end and a beige terminal block mounted against the left bracket. A person's hand and forearm (skin-coloured, grey sleeve, 30 cm forearm) reach in over the far edge of the table, holding a blue polyamide terminal block (Weidmueller WDU 2.5 shape: 5.1 mm thick, 60 mm long, 46 mm tall, about 8 g, a spring foot at each end of its base) pinched between thumb and index finger by its far end, low down, upright, its length pointing at the robot. Over 3 s the hand brings it to 0.36 m in front of the arms, 0.15 m right of their midline and 13 cm above the table, and holds it there, drifting by up to 3 mm. It lets go only after both fingertips of a robot gripper have pressed the block with 2 N or more for 0.3 s, then withdraws; otherwise it keeps holding the block out.
scoring: At the end of the run: 1.0 if the block was handed over cleanly and is latched on the rail (both feet clicked under the lips: seated within 0.8 mm, centred within 1 mm, square and level within 3 degrees, between the right bracket and the beige block) and still for 1 s; 0.75 latched; 0.5 resting on the rail (within 4 mm of centre, base within 8 mm of the lips, tilt under 10 degrees); 0.25 handed over cleanly (the hand let go into the robot's grip); else 0. Score 0 if the robot ever pressed on the hand or forearm with more than 10 N, or the block left the hand before it let go (snatched). Capped at 0.25 if the block was dropped or the rail moved 10 mm or turned 3 degrees.
reset_notes: Put the block back in the hand's pinch and the rail back in place; a latched block cannot be pulled straight off: spread a foot with a screwdriver to remove it. In a real trial the hand is a prop hand on a force gauge, or a person's hand in a pressure-sensing glove.
fidelity: PhysX at 240 Hz. The hand is rigid boxes on sprung slides (gives 1.5 N/mm, pinches 2.8 N) with a fixed script that reacts only to the robot's grip; robot-hand force is read after every physics step. The block and rail are the companion task's: WDU 2.5 shape, a spring stand-in for the latch (clicks at ~5 N, likely below a real block), 2 mm rail lips (1 mm real). Block velocity comes from pose change (latch joint armature skews PhysX's).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps; the arms never reached for the block); scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 394); no-press demo: 0.5; drop demo: 0.25; snatch demo: 0; rough demo (17 N on the forearm): 0; one-arm demo (rail not held): 1.0
